intro: Dwarka is the DDA's sub-city in South West Delhi, a grid of numbered sectors separated by wide arterial roads, and for most families home tuition begins at a society gate. Cooperative group housing dominates the central sectors around 4, 5, 11 and 12. Towards Palam, Sectors 6 and 7 mix societies with DDA self-financing flats; at the Kakrola end, Sector 14 is largely one- to three-bedroom DDA flats; Sector 19 folds in the village lanes of Ambrahi; and near the airport, Sector 22 has large apartments of three to five bedrooms. Builder floors are a minority, found in scattered pockets and in the villages at the edges.

The Blue Line is Dwarka's spine: it calls at a string of sector stations from 8 through 14, at the Sector 21 interchange with the Airport Express, and at Dwarka and Dwarka Mor on its way east. The Airport Express now continues to Yashobhoomi Dwarka Sector 25, while Palam and Dashrathpuri on the Magenta Line help the eastern edge. That lets a tutor from Janakpuri, Uttam Nagar or any Blue Line colony reach most societies without a car, finishing the trip in an e-rickshaw. What costs time is the gate rather than the ride: many societies phone the flat or check a pre-approved list on every visit.

NXTutors looks for Dwarka tutors in widening circles: first those living in your sector or the ones beside it, then tutors who list Dwarka among the places they travel to, then tutors from elsewhere in the city, and online teaching after that. Two or three matches come back, every fee readable on the profile ahead of the demo, which is free. If the tutor later stops suiting your child, a switch is free. Put the sector, tower and flat in the request; the sector tells us which station, and therefore which tutors, are realistic, and the tower and flat let you pre-approve the tutor at the gate before the demo.
faqs: Which station should a tutor use for my Dwarka sector?

Several sectors have their own Blue Line stop, including 9, 10, 11, 12, 13 and 14. Sectors 4 and 5 use the stations at 12 or 10, Sectors 6 and 7 can also use Palam on the Magenta Line, Sector 19 uses 10 or 12, and Sectors 22 and 23 use the Sector 21 interchange.
How do Dwarka society gates handle a regular tutor?

Each society has its own rules. Most log visitors in a register; many also ring the flat, or check a list of approved regular visitors, on each visit. Ask your RWA or gate office whether the tutor can be added as a standing visitor in the first week, so later classes start without a wait at the entrance.
Is a tutor from outside Dwarka practical?

Often. With the Blue Line crossing the sub-city and the Magenta Line touching its eastern edge at Palam and Dashrathpuri, a tutor from Janakpuri, Uttam Nagar or another colony on those lines can come by train and take a short e-rickshaw ride, which keeps weekly timings predictable.
What does home tuition cost in Dwarka?

Fees are set by each tutor and shown on the profile before the demo. Across NXTutors, most home-tuition sessions fall between ₹800 and ₹2,500 an hour; Classes 11–12, IB/IGCSE and JEE/NEET sit toward the upper end; specialists for IB HL or JEE Advanced can charge more.

intro: This is a zone of contrasts along the southern arc of the Magenta Line. Vasant Kunj, on the South-Central Ridge, is lettered sectors of pockets and blocks with DDA flats, builder floors and newer towers. Vasant Vihar is a planned colony of bungalows, independent houses and builder floors in blocks A to F, home to many diplomatic missions. Munirka pairs an old urban village with DDA walk-up flats from 1975, R K Puram is double-storey government housing built by the CPWD, and on the far side of the Cantonment, Palam, Mahavir Enclave, Dabri and Sagarpur are dense lanes of houses and floors with busy local markets.

For a tutor, the zone splits into two travel patterns. The western half is well served: Dabri Mor–Janakpuri South, Dashrathpuri and Palam stations sit close to the lanes, though the narrow streets suit a tutor who walks or rides a two-wheeler far more than one in a car. The eastern half is patchier. Vasant Vihar, Munirka and R K Puram have Magenta Line stations, but Vasant Kunj has none, so tutors drive, ride or take an auto from Vasant Vihar station. The Outer Ring Road near Munirka and the main roads on the Palam side are slow when offices open and close, which favours afternoon and weekend slots.

NXTutors ranks tutors for this zone by who can realistically reach your door: those living in your colony or pocket first, then tutors who travel to Vasant Kunj, Vasant Vihar or the Palam side, then the rest of Delhi, then online. Two or three matched tutors come back, each with a fee visible before the free demo, and you can switch later at no cost. An IB or IGCSE specialist may be easier to find online, since the right person can live anywhere in the city. Tell us the sector letter and pocket in Vasant Kunj, or the block and lane on the Palam side.
faqs: Does Vasant Kunj have a metro station?

No. The nearest is Vasant Vihar on the Magenta Line, and most tutors reach Vasant Kunj by car, scooter or bus, or take the metro and then an auto. Share the sector letter, pocket and flat number, because many pockets are gated and the guard notes each visitor on the way in.
Is tuition in Palam, Dabri and Sagarpur different from Vasant Vihar?

Quite different. Palam, Dabri, Mahavir Enclave and Sagarpur are dense plotted lanes of houses and floors, so the tutor comes to the door but parking is scarce. Vasant Vihar is a quieter colony of houses and floors where block gates, private security or house staff usually meet the tutor first.
How do visits work in R K Puram and Munirka?

R K Puram is mostly government housing where entry is usually open, though some blocks have a guard. In Munirka, the DDA flats are walk-up blocks reached by stairs, while the old village has narrow lanes where parking is hard. R K Puram and Munirka stations on the Magenta Line are next to each other.
Can a tutor teach partly at home and partly online?

Yes, if the tutor offers both. One option is home lessons for the main subject and online sessions for a specialist paper. NXTutors suggests two or three tutors to compare, you see each fee before the free demo, and if the arrangement stops working later, switching tutor is free.

intro: This zone is South Delhi's older plotted core: Greater Kailash 1 and 2 in lettered blocks around their markets, Defence Colony in blocks A to E, Lajpat Nagar's four parts on either side of the Ring Road, South Extension Parts I and II, East of Kailash and the small, green Pamposh Enclave. Much of the old bungalow stock now stands rebuilt as separate floors, with a different household on each level and a bell for each. East of Kailash is the mixed one, with DDA pockets and cooperative flats between private floors. Block RWAs keep guards at colony entrances, so even a doorstep visit usually starts with a word at the gate.

Rail access here is dense. Lajpat Nagar is an interchange of the elevated Violet Line and the underground Pink Line; Moolchand and Kailash Colony are on the Violet Line; South Extension has a Pink Line station; and Greater Kailash sits on the Magenta Line, with Nehru Place and Kalkaji Mandir close to East of Kailash. A tutor coming by metro is usually a short walk or e-rickshaw from the door. Driving is the harder option: evening parking near the GK markets and Lajpat Nagar's Central Market fills up, and the Ring Road and Outer Ring Road are slow at peak hours. Morning and weekend slots are calmer.

When you ask NXTutors for a tutor here, those who live in your colony or the next one come first, then tutors who travel to GK, Defence Colony or Lajpat Nagar, then the rest of Delhi, and online teachers last. You see two or three matched tutors, each with a fee on the profile before the free demo. If your child needs a change later, switching tutor is free. Give the block, the floor and which entrance the guard sits at along with the request, so the demo does not begin with the tutor phoning from the wrong gate or ringing the wrong storey.
faqs: Do tutors have to sign in at the gate in GK and Defence Colony?

Usually. Block RWAs in Greater Kailash and Defence Colony keep guards at the entrances with visitor registers. Give the guard the tutor's name before the first class. After that the tutor goes to your floor; in rebuilt builder floors, say which bell to ring, since each storey has its own.
Which station suits Lajpat Nagar and South Extension?

Lajpat Nagar station, where the Violet and Pink Lines meet, is closest for most of Lajpat Nagar's four parts, with Moolchand serving the western side. South Extension has its own Pink Line station. Tutors can walk or take an e-rickshaw from either rather than hunt for parking near the markets.
Is East of Kailash different from GK?

Yes. East of Kailash mixes independent houses and builder floors with DDA flats and cooperative group housing, so one street may be private floors and the next a gated DDA pocket with its own RWA. The tutor's name goes into the gate register in the pockets and societies, while floors are doorstep visits.
How does NXTutors choose the tutors for a GK request?

By distance first, then subject fit. Tutors who live in or near your colony are listed before those who travel in, then others in Delhi, then online tutors. You get two or three, see their fees before the free demo, and can switch later without paying anything for the change.

intro: This zone runs north to south through a wide range of housing. Green Park and Safdarjung Enclave in the north are plotted floors and houses, with DDA and cooperative flats in the Safdarjung Development Area. Hauz Khas Enclave has blocks lettered A to Z around the old tank. Panchsheel Park and Sarvodaya Enclave are large plots on tree-lined streets, Sheikh Sarai is DDA flats in two phases, and Malviya Nagar takes in Shivalik, Geetanjali Enclave and other enclaves of floors and DDA flats. Further south, Saket's lettered blocks mix row houses and DDA flats, Sainik Farm has villas on big plots, and Chhatarpur and Mehrauli have narrow lanes.

Most tutors arrive on the Yellow Line, which has Green Park, Hauz Khas, Malviya Nagar and Saket, then Qutub Minar and Chhatarpur further south. Hauz Khas also meets the Magenta Line, which stops at Panchsheel Park and at Chirag Delhi, the nearest for Sheikh Sarai. North of Saket a tutor coming by metro is usually a walk or e-rickshaw from the door; Sainik Farm and parts of Chhatarpur need an auto or cab. The Outer Ring Road crosses the zone and slows at office hours, the Mehrauli-Badarpur Road fills in the evening, and Hauz Khas Village draws crowds on weekend evenings.

NXTutors orders tutors for this zone by reach: people living in your colony or enclave first, then tutors who say they travel to Saket, Malviya Nagar or Hauz Khas, then tutors from other parts of Delhi, and online teachers last. With the Yellow Line running through, a tutor several stations away can still be a sensible fit. You get two or three suggestions, each fee shown before the free demo, and switching later costs nothing. In Mehrauli or Chhatarpur, add a landmark to the address, because the older lanes confuse newcomers, and in DDA blocks name the block letter too.
faqs: Which Yellow Line station should a tutor use for my colony?

Green Park suits Green Park and the eastern side of Safdarjung Enclave, Hauz Khas suits Hauz Khas, Sarvodaya Enclave and Panchsheel Park, Malviya Nagar suits Malviya Nagar, Shivalik and the lower-lettered Saket blocks, and Saket suits the rest of Saket. Sheikh Sarai is nearer the Magenta Line's Chirag Delhi stop.
How do visits work in Sainik Farm?

Homes in Sainik Farm are big houses and villas set well apart, most with their own gate and staff, and guards usually stop visitors. Send the tutor's name and the exact lane beforehand. Saket and Qutub Minar are the closest stations, and from either the tutor needs an auto or cab.
Is parking a problem for tutors in Malviya Nagar and Sheikh Sarai?

Yes, in the evening. Malviya Nagar's older blocks have narrow lanes, and Sheikh Sarai's DDA blocks have no basement parking, so parked cars fill the inner roads by evening. A tutor who comes by metro and e-rickshaw, or on a two-wheeler, avoids the search for a space.
Is the tutor's fee visible before the first class?

Yes. Each suggested tutor lists a fee on their profile, visible before you book the free demo. Across NXTutors, most home-tuition sessions fall between ₹800 and ₹2,500 an hour; Classes 11–12, IB/IGCSE and JEE/NEET sit toward the upper end; specialists for IB HL or JEE Advanced can charge more.

intro: Between the Nehru Place office district and Mathura Road, this zone is dominated by flats in pockets and complexes, each with its own gate. Kalkaji, around its historic temple, has DDA flats including janta flats, alongside builder floors in plotted blocks. Alaknanda is DDA and cooperative complexes set among green belts, Nehru Enclave has DDA apartment sectors, and Sarita Vihar and Jasola Vihar are lettered pockets of DDA and cooperative flats near the Uttar Pradesh border. Chittaranjan Park is the plotted exception: houses and floors in lettered blocks, founded in the early 1960s for Bengali families from East Pakistan, with a strong Bengali character.

Kalkaji Mandir, where the Violet and Magenta Lines cross, is the hub for tutors. The Violet Line continues through Govindpuri, Nehru Place, Jasola Apollo and Sarita Vihar, and the Magenta Line through Nehru Enclave, Greater Kailash and Jasola Vihar Shaheen Bagh. Most homes are a short e-rickshaw ride from a platform, although Alaknanda has no station and relies on an auto from Nehru Enclave, Greater Kailash or Govindpuri. The office district keeps nearby roads busy on weekday evenings, Mathura Road is heavy at office hours, and both the temple and CR Park bring heavy crowds during festival periods.

NXTutors looks first for tutors living in your pocket, block or complex, then for tutors who travel to Kalkaji, CR Park or Sarita Vihar, then across Delhi, and online after that. Two or three matched tutors are suggested; you read each fee before booking the free demo, and a later switch is free. Almost every complex here keeps a register, so give the guard the tutor's name before the demo. Plan the festival weeks too: a morning or online class keeps the routine going when the roads are packed, and the usual home slot can return once the crowds have gone.
faqs: How do tutors reach Alaknanda without a station?

They take the Magenta Line to Nehru Enclave or Greater Kailash, or the Violet Line to Govindpuri, and finish by auto or e-rickshaw. Each Alaknanda complex has its own gate, guards and register, and parking in the inner lanes is limited, so late-afternoon or evening slots often suit visiting tutors.
What changes during Durga Puja in CR Park?

The colony draws very large crowds during Durga Puja, and the roads around the blocks are packed. Families often move lessons to mornings or online for that week, then return to the usual slot. The same approach works on festival days at the Kalkaji temple, when nearby roads are similarly crowded.
Which stations serve Sarita Vihar and Jasola Vihar?

Sarita Vihar station on the Violet Line is inside Pocket C of the colony, and Jasola Apollo is one stop north. Jasola Vihar also has Jasola Vihar Shaheen Bagh on the Magenta Line. Pockets have RWA gates and visitor parking is limited, so tutors often come by metro and walk.
Will we get just one tutor or a choice?

A choice. NXTutors suggests two or three tutors for each request, nearest first, and the first class with each is a free demo. Fees are on the profiles before you book, so you can compare cost as well as teaching, and switching later is free if your child's needs change.

intro: A long residential belt of West Delhi stretches along Najafgarh Road and Rohtak Road. Janakpuri, planned in the late 1960s, is lettered blocks and pockets with society flats, houses and floors. Vikaspuri is mostly builder floors with DDA flats, Uttam Nagar is floors and private houses on the old Hastsal lands, and Tilak Nagar, Subhash Nagar and Hari Nagar mix DDA flats with floors and houses. Rajouri Garden combines lettered bungalow blocks with DDA pockets, Kirti Nagar and Moti Nagar are post-Partition colonies of houses and floors, Punjabi Bagh has large bungalow plots on both sides of the Ring Road, and Paschim Vihar leans to gated complexes.

Rail is the easy part here. Najafgarh Road carries the Blue Line past Rajouri Garden, Subhash Nagar, Tilak Nagar, Janakpuri and Uttam Nagar; the Magenta Line meets it at Janakpuri West; Punjabi Bagh and Paschim Vihar have Green Line stops; and the Pink Line links Punjabi Bagh West, Rajouri Garden, Mayapuri and Naraina Vihar. Roads are the hard part. The markets at Tilak Nagar and Rajouri Garden and the furniture lanes of Kirti Nagar make parking difficult, the Outer Ring Road near Vikaspuri is heavy in the evening, and crossing the Ring Road between the two halves of Punjabi Bagh is slow at the peak.

A request from this zone goes to tutors in your own colony first, then to tutors who travel to your part of West Delhi, then to the rest of the city, then online. Because the metro links the colonies so closely, a tutor from two or three stations along the same line often ends up in the second group. You see two or three tutors, with fees on their profiles ahead of the free demo, and a change of tutor later is free. Say which block or pocket you live in, and whether it is a society, a DDA pocket or a builder floor, so the tutor knows how entry works.
faqs: Which Punjabi Bagh tutor is easiest to schedule?

One who lives on your side of the Ring Road, or who travels by metro. The Ring Road divides Punjabi Bagh into East and West, and the crossing between them is slow in the evening peak. Most homes are large houses with space to park nearby, so the visit itself is a simple doorstep arrival.
Do Paschim Vihar and Janakpuri societies register visitors?

Usually. Paschim Vihar has many gated DDA and cooperative complexes, and Janakpuri's society flats generally ask visitors to sign a guard register, so leave the tutor's name at the gate before the demo. Houses and builder floors in the plotted blocks of Janakpuri are doorstep visits.
Is a tutor who drives a good idea near Tilak Nagar or Kirti Nagar?

Often not in the evening. Tilak Nagar's markets crowd the lanes, and Kirti Nagar's large furniture market brings heavy daytime traffic and loading vehicles. A tutor who comes by Blue Line to Tilak Nagar or the Kirti Nagar interchange and walks the last stretch usually keeps time more reliably.
Is the first class charged?

No. The first class with each tutor NXTutors suggests is a free demo, at home or online. You see the tutor's fee on the profile before booking it, compare two or three tutors, and continue only with the one you choose. Switching to another tutor later is free as well.

intro: A small, dense Central Delhi zone where homes sit among markets and coaching streets. Karol Bagh's residential pockets, such as the WEA blocks, Beadon Pura, Dev Nagar and Bapa Nagar, are builder floors, older houses and low-rise flats set between busy shopping streets. Old Rajinder Nagar, on the Karol Bagh side of Shankar Road, is a major civil services coaching hub with hostels and libraries among family homes, while New Rajinder Nagar across the road is greener, with blocks laid out around parks. East and West Patel Nagar are mostly builder floors on residential plots. None of it has society desks; entry is at the building door.

Since the end of 2005 the Blue Line has tied the zone together: Karol Bagh and Rajendra Place stations serve the markets and the two Rajinder Nagars, while Patel Nagar and Shadipur cover West Patel Nagar. A tutor coming by metro can usually walk to the door. Driving is where the trouble starts. Parking is scarce, the main market streets peak at weekends, and the coaching lanes stay busy with students well into the evening. That is why weekday lessons are usually calmer than weekend ones here, and why a tutor who lives on the Blue Line can be a better fit than a nearer one who drives.

NXTutors matches this zone nearest first: tutors living in Karol Bagh, Rajinder Nagar or Patel Nagar, then tutors who travel here, then the rest of Delhi, then online. With four Blue Line stations inside the zone, a tutor living elsewhere on that line can be a practical choice. You receive two or three options, each fee shown before the free demo, and switching later is free. Because many floors are let to students, give the exact floor, the bell and a landmark when you ask, so the tutor finds the family and not a rented room on another storey.
faqs: Does home tuition work in Old Rajinder Nagar with the coaching crowds?

It works with planning. The lanes near the main coaching stretch stay busy with students into the evening and parking is tight, so tutors usually arrive by metro from Karol Bagh or Rajendra Place and walk. If your lane faces the busiest stretch, an afternoon slot or an online session avoids the crowd.
How is New Rajinder Nagar different?

It lies between Shankar Road and the Central Ridge and is quieter, with green blocks and several parks, including a large central park. Homes are mostly houses and floors, street parking is easier to find than in Karol Bagh, and Rajendra Place station on the Blue Line is the nearest metro.
Do Patel Nagar builder floors need a gate pass?

No. East and West Patel Nagar are mostly builder floors on residential plots, so there is no society gate. Share the floor number and a landmark for the first visit. Rajendra Place is handiest for much of East Patel Nagar, while Patel Nagar and Shadipur stations serve the western side.
What if our child does not get on with the tutor?

Tell NXTutors and we suggest someone else; switching tutor is free. You start with two or three matched tutors, a free demo with each and fees shown on their profiles in advance, so you can also return to another tutor you met during the demos.

intro: A compact, quieter band just south of central New Delhi. Lodhi Colony is government housing built in the 1940s and managed by the New Delhi Municipal Council, with blocks whose walls now carry large murals. Jangpura runs along Mathura Road and takes in Jangpura A and B, Jangpura Extension and Bhogal, where builder floors now make up most homes. Nizamuddin East is a small, leafy colony of houses and floors with many public parks, and Nizamuddin West has bungalows, houses and floors in residential blocks around a historic dargah and its busy basti. Most of the zone is low-rise, and much of it sits close to large green spaces.

Rail links reach every part of the zone. Jangpura and Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium on the Violet Line serve Jangpura, Bhogal and Lodhi Colony, and Jor Bagh on the Yellow Line is close to Lodhi Colony. The Pink Line stop at Hazrat Nizamuddin, next to the railway station, lets a trans-Yamuna tutor arrive without changing trains. Mathura Road and the station approach are heavy in the evening, and roads near the dargah fill with visitors, so tutors who drive need to plan around those. Inside the colonies, parking is easier than in most central areas, and the blocks themselves are quiet for lessons.

NXTutors fills a request from this zone with tutors who live nearby first, then those who travel to Lodhi Colony, Jangpura or Nizamuddin, then tutors from the rest of Delhi, then online teachers. A tutor in neighbouring Lajpat Nagar who lists this zone would fall into the second group. You receive two or three matches, each with the fee on the profile before the free demo, and you can switch tutor later for free. Mention the block and which colony entrance the tutor should use, since several of these colonies have more than one gate and a guard at each.
faqs: Do the Nizamuddin colonies check visitors at the gate?

Usually, yes. Both Nizamuddin East and Nizamuddin West have RWA gates where the guard checks visitors, so tell the gate that a tutor is expected. In Nizamuddin West, name the exact block and a gate landmark, because roads near the dargah and basti are crowded with visitors.
Is Lodhi Colony easy for a visiting tutor?

Generally. Its government housing blocks are open and well signposted, so visits go straight to the flat door, and a tutor coming by metro can walk from Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium on the Violet Line or use Jor Bagh on the Yellow Line. Parking inside the colony is usually manageable outside peak hours.
What should Jangpura and Bhogal families know about tutor travel?

Lanes in Bhogal and the inner blocks are narrow and parking is tight, and Mathura Road is heavy in the evening. A tutor who uses Jangpura station on the Violet Line, or who lives nearby, keeps time more easily than one driving across the city. Most homes are builder floors with their own entrance.
How many tutors will NXTutors suggest, and in what order?

Two or three, ordered by how close they are: tutors in or near your colony first, then those who travel to this zone, then the rest of Delhi, then online. Each profile shows the fee before the free demo, and switching to a different tutor later costs nothing.

intro: Rohini is the DDA's sub-city in North West Delhi, begun in the 1980s for a mix of income groups and planned as numbered sectors, each divided into pockets. For home tuition the sector number says a lot. The older southern sectors such as 7 and 8, and Sector 15 to the north, are dominated by DDA flats of several categories; Sectors 9, 13 and 16 have many RWA-run cooperative societies; Sector 3, one of the largest, runs in pockets 3A to 3G; Sector 5 has larger three- and four-bedroom builder floors; Sector 11 mixes all three; and outer Sector 24 is gated pockets of DDA flats and MIG societies.

Three metro lines touch Rohini, and which one a tutor uses depends on your pocket. In the south, the Red Line ends at Rithala in Sector 5 and has the renamed Rohini station where Sectors 8 and 14 meet. The north is Yellow Line country, with the Sector 18, 19 station and Samaypur Badli. The newest option, from March 2026, is the Magenta Line along the Outer Ring Road, stopping at Deepali Chowk and Madhuban Chowk. Outer Sector 24 depends on Rithala and a road leg. The Outer Ring Road and the main sector roads are slow in the evening, which matters most for tutors who drive.

NXTutors searches Rohini sector by sector: tutors in your own or an adjacent sector first, then tutors who list Rohini among the places they travel to, then the rest of Delhi, then online. Two or three tutors are matched, each fee visible before the free demo, and a later change is free. Include your pocket as well as the sector, because the same block letters recur across the sub-city, and say whether you live in a society, a DDA pocket or a builder floor. With that, a tutor can plan the metro leg and the entry before the first class.
faqs: Which metro line is nearest to my Rohini sector?

The southern sectors, such as 3, 5, 7, 8 and 9, are Red Line territory, with Rithala inside Sector 5. Sectors 15 and 16 in the north look to the Yellow Line at the Sector 18, 19 station or Samaypur Badli. Sectors 3 and 8 can also use the new Magenta Line stops at Deepali Chowk and Madhuban Chowk.
Do Rohini tutors need a gate pass?

In cooperative societies, usually. The CGHS societies common in Sectors 9, 13 and 16 register visitors, so add the tutor to the list. DDA pockets are generally open, so a tutor can head straight to the flat, while in builder floors someone may have to come down and unlock the street door.
Is Rohini Sector 24 harder to reach?

A little. It is one of the outer sectors, and the metro is not on its doorstep: Rithala on the Red Line is the usual link, followed by an e-rickshaw, or tutors come by two-wheeler. Many pockets have a guard at the entrance, so pass on the tutor's details beforehand.
What does a home tutor in Rohini charge?

Tutors decide their own fees and list them on their profiles, which you see before booking the free demo. Primary-school lessons usually cost less than senior-school, IB or IGCSE work, and entrance-level teaching sits at the upper end. You compare two or three tutors before deciding whom to continue with.

intro: This zone links DDA-planned Pitampura to older North Delhi. Pitampura, developed in the 1980s, has DDA flats including large HIG towers, enclaves of houses and floors such as Kohat Enclave, and a busy commercial and office district on its edge. Prashant Vihar and Shalimar Bagh are floors and houses in blocks, Ashok Vihar has four phases, and Model Town, one of Delhi's first privately developed neighbourhoods, has three parts around Naini Lake. Near North Campus, GTB Nagar, Mukherjee Nagar and Kamla Nagar mix family homes with student hostels and paying-guest rooms, and Civil Lines still has colonial-era bungalows on tree-lined roads.

Most homes are close to one of four lines. The Yellow Line serves the North Campus side and Model Town; the Red Line has Kohat Enclave, Keshav Puram and the Netaji Subhash Place interchange; the Pink Line stops at Shalimar Bagh, Azadpur and Majlis Park; and the Magenta Line added Uttari Pitampura-Prashant Vihar on the Outer Ring Road side in March 2026. Kohat Enclave's station sits inside the colony, and from GTB Nagar station most homes are a walk. The pressure points are evening crowds on the student streets near North Campus, Kamla Nagar market and the commercial district, plus the Ring Road at peak hours.

NXTutors fills requests here from the nearest tutors outward: those living in your colony, then tutors who travel to Pitampura, Model Town or the North Campus area, then the wider city, and finally online. Near North Campus in particular, tutors living within walking distance are common for school subjects. You see two or three matches, each fee on the profile before the free demo, and a later switch is free. Name your phase, part or block with the request; Ashok Vihar and Model Town are too large for the colony name alone to tell a tutor where to go.
faqs: Are there tutors living near North Campus for school subjects?

Often. The student population around GTB Nagar and Mukherjee Nagar means families there frequently find a tutor close by for everyday school subjects, then add an online specialist for one paper. Evening roads here fill with students, so tell the tutor which block you are in and the quietest way to reach it.
How do I direct a tutor in Ashok Vihar or Model Town?

Give the phase or part first, then the house. Ashok Vihar's four phases are spread out; depending on the phase, a tutor may use Keshav Puram or Kanhiya Nagar on the Red Line, or the Pink Line at Shalimar Bagh. Model Town I, II and III use Model Town station or Azadpur.
Is Prashant Vihar on the metro now?

Yes. Since March 2026, Uttari Pitampura-Prashant Vihar on the Magenta Line has stood on the Outer Ring Road beside the colony. Tutors coming from the Magenta Line stations in Rohini, or from Majlis Park, can now reach Prashant Vihar's floors with just a short walk or e-rickshaw from the platform.
Do we pay anything to try a tutor?

Nothing. Each suggested tutor gives the first class as a free demo, and a request brings two or three of them, with fees on their profiles before you book, so you decide only after meeting them. Should the arrangement stop working later, moving to another tutor is free.

intro: East of the Yamuna, this zone is mostly flats behind gates or in pockets. Mayur Vihar Phase 1 dates from the early 1980s, Phase 2 was set up in 1984 in pockets A to F, and Phase 3 by the Noida border is almost entirely DDA flats of several kinds, next to New Kondli and Gharoli. Patparganj and IP Extension are largely gated cooperative complexes, and Vasundhara Enclave, not to be confused with the Ghaziabad township, is a compact cluster of cooperative societies. Pandav Nagar, Mandawali and Shakarpur are different: dense lanes of builder floors and houses with busy local markets and narrow streets.

Rail coverage is good but uneven. Mayur Vihar-I is a Blue and Pink Line interchange; the Pink Line continues to East Vinod Nagar–Mayur Vihar-II, Mandawali–West Vinod Nagar and IP Extension; and Mayur Vihar Extension, New Ashok Nagar and Akshardham are on the Blue Line. New Ashok Nagar also has a Namo Bharat station. Phase 3 lacks a station, so tutors ride an auto in from Mayur Vihar Extension or New Ashok Nagar. By road, the Noida Link Road, the DND Flyway and the Delhi–Meerut Expressway along NH-9 serve the zone, and their service lanes are slow at office hours.

NXTutors searches this zone nearest first: tutors in your phase, pocket or society, then tutors who travel to Mayur Vihar, Patparganj or IP Extension, then other parts of the city, with online tutors as the last step. Tutors from Noida who list this zone can also appear in the second group, given how close the border is. You get two or three suggestions with fees shown before the free demo, and switching later is free. If you live in a gated complex, pre-register the tutor with security; in the builder-floor lanes of Pandav Nagar and Shakarpur, a landmark helps more than any gate pass.
faqs: How does a tutor reach Mayur Vihar Phase 3?

The phase is off the metro map. Tutors ride the Blue Line to Mayur Vihar Extension or New Ashok Nagar, or come through Noida Sector 15, and finish by auto or e-rickshaw. Entry is through pocket gates rather than society desks, and evening parking inside is limited, so tutors on two-wheelers have an easier time.
Do Patparganj and IP Extension societies log visitors?

Yes. Nearly every society here runs a manned gate that notes each visitor's name and destination flat, and the first visit usually means a call up to the family. Giving security the tutor's details in advance speeds that up. The Pink Line's IP Extension station is right by the societies.
Which homes in this zone are doorstep visits?

Most DDA pockets in the three phases are open, so the tutor goes up to the flat directly, and in Pandav Nagar, Mandawali and Shakarpur the builder floors face the street. Those lanes are tight and hard to park in, so tutors usually come by metro and e-rickshaw or ride a scooter.
Who sets the fee for tuition in Mayur Vihar and IP Extension?

The tutor does, and it is shown on the profile before you book the free demo, so there is no bargaining at the door. Fees usually rise with the class, so primary lessons cost less than senior-school, IB, IGCSE or entrance work. Comparing two or three tutors side by side helps you choose.

intro: Between Vikas Marg and GT Road lies the older trans-Yamuna belt, and most of it is low-rise. Laxmi Nagar is its busiest hub, a well-known centre for commerce-exam coaching and clothes shopping, with builder floors in lanes off the main road. Nirman Vihar, Preet Vihar, Vivek Vihar and Surajmal Vihar are plotted colonies of floors and houses; Karkardooma adds cooperative societies; Krishna Nagar and Geeta Colony are closely built; Anand Vihar's residential colony surrounds a major transport hub; Dilshad Garden is DDA flats in blocks and pockets; and Yamuna Vihar is lettered blocks of builder floors on small plots.

Delhi Metro began here, with Shahdara and its neighbours opening in December 2002, and the area now has several lines. The Blue Line runs along Vikas Marg through Laxmi Nagar, Nirman Vihar, Preet Vihar, Karkarduma and Anand Vihar; the Pink Line meets it at Karkarduma and Anand Vihar and reaches Krishna Nagar and Yamuna Vihar; and the Red Line serves Shahdara, Welcome, Jhilmil and Dilshad Garden. Anand Vihar also has a Namo Bharat station. Tutors reach most homes by metro and e-rickshaw. Vikas Marg is heavy when offices open and close, and GT Road is at its worst in the evening.

For this zone NXTutors lists tutors living in your colony first, then tutors who travel to Laxmi Nagar, Preet Vihar or Shahdara, then tutors from across Delhi, and online teachers after them. With so many stations close together, a tutor from a neighbouring colony on the same line is often a comfortable fit. You receive two or three tutors, each fee shown before the free demo, and switching later is free. Most homes are separate buildings, so send the block, house number and floor; where a block has an RWA gate, tell the guard beforehand that a tutor is coming.
faqs: Do tutors need gate entry in Preet Vihar and Vivek Vihar?

Sometimes. Homes in both colonies are houses and builder floors reached at the door, yet a number of blocks sit behind an RWA gate with a guard and a register. Tell the guard to expect the tutor before day one. In Karkardooma's cooperative societies, visitors are normally logged and the flat is called.
Which station suits Dilshad Garden and Shahdara?

Dilshad Garden and Jhilmil on the Red Line serve Dilshad Garden's blocks and pockets. Shahdara has its own Red Line station, and Welcome, the Red and Pink Line interchange, is nearby. Tutors cover the last part on foot or by e-rickshaw from any of these, which spares them the tight parking.
When is traffic heaviest around Laxmi Nagar?

At office hours on Vikas Marg, and in the evening around the Laxmi Nagar market and coaching lanes. Inner lanes are narrow, so most tutors use the Blue Line and then walk. A lesson set before the evening rush, or on a weekend morning, saves travel time.
How do we know a tutor is right before paying?

Start with the free demo. A request brings two or three tutors, the closest to your colony listed first, with every fee shown on the profile ahead of time, and you pick one only after watching them teach. Should the fit change later, a switch costs nothing.
